metadata.archetype_justification: The application has a PostgreSQL database with CRUD ticket operations (list, search), user-specific data via Django auth middleware, and persistent state management. No message queue consumers, no multi-service orchestration, and no event-processing patterns were found. Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.15 yields Not Ready band but 10 High findings (< 12) maps to Remediation Required tier. The score is extremely low because nearly every question scores 1, but the count-based rule requires ≥12 High for Not Ready. The count-based tier is authoritative. The divergence reflects that while nearly every dimension is inadequate, the system's small scope means remediation is feasible.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance with Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi on Ubuntu 12.04 (EOL). No managed container orchestration or serverless is in use.
findings.gap: No managed compute services. Single EC2 instance with no container orchestration, no serverless, and no managed WSGI platform.
findings.recommendation: Containerize the application and deploy on ECS with Fargate, or migrate to Lambda with API Gateway.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 runs self-managed on the same EC2 instance as the application. No managed database service is used.
findings.gap: Database is entirely self-managed with no automated failover, no managed patching, and no separation from compute.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (latest supported version).

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. All logic inline in view functions. For a stateful-crud service, future ticket lifecycle workflows would need orchestration.
findings.gap: No orchestration — all workflow logic hardcoded in application code.
findings.recommendation: If ticket lifecycle management grows in complexity, adopt AWS Step Functions for multi-step coordination.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. Email notifications via synchronous SMTP relay block the request thread. For a stateful-crud service, managed messaging for notifications and state changes is expected.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes should trigger notifications asynchronously. Email sending blocks the request path.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Amazon SQS or SNS for asynchronous email notifications.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network security configuration defined in repository. No IaC for VPC, subnets, security groups, or NACLs.
findings.gap: No network security definition. Cannot verify VPC isolation, subnet placement, or security group configuration.
findings.recommendation: Define network infrastructure in IaC: VPC with private subnets, security groups with least-privilege rules, proper segmentation.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or any managed entry point. Application served directly by Apache on EC2.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly with no gateway or load balancer. No throttling, no edge authentication, no DDoS protection.
findings.recommendation: Add an ALB or API Gateway as entry point with throttling and authentication.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configured. Single EC2 instance with static capacity.
findings.gap: All capacity statically provisioned on a single instance. Cannot respond to traffic spikes.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to managed compute, configure auto-scaling with appropriate min/max capacity.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: Only backup is a daily pg_dump cron job. No automated backup configuration, no PITR, no tested restore procedures.
findings.gap: No managed backup solution. Daily pg_dump with no retention policy, no PITR, no tested restore.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS PostgreSQL with automated backups and point-in-time recovery.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: All resources on single EC2 instance in single AZ. Application and database co-located — AZ failure takes down entire system.
findings.gap: Single AZ deployment with no fault isolation. No multi-AZ, no failover mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Deploy across multiple AZs: RDS with Multi-AZ, ECS/Fargate tasks via ALB across AZs.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No Infrastructure as Code exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any IaC definitions. All infrastructure manually created.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage — all infrastructure manually provisioned (ClickOps).
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in Terraform or CDK: VPC, compute, database, and operational resources.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is manual git pull + Apache restart. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments are manual with no quality gates or rollback capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodePipeline) with lint, test, build, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Python 2.7 (EOL Jan 2020) with Django 1.4 (EOL 2015). Compound legacy: both language version AND framework are severely regressed. No AWS SDK usage.
findings.gap: End-of-life language and framework. No security patches available. No modern AWS SDK support.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Python 3.12+ with Django 5.x or FastAPI. This is a prerequisite for all other modernization.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries. 2 Python files with all functionality in a single deployable unit. No separation between business logic, data access, and presentation.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with pervasive shared state. No module boundaries, no separation of concerns.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Conditional/Adaptive approach: containerize as-is, then restructure with proper separation. Full decomposition not warranted for current scope.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP. Email via synchronous SMTP blocks request thread. For a stateful-crud service, async patterns for cross-service state propagation would be expected.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns. Email sending blocks request processing.
findings.recommendation: Adopt SQS/SNS for ticket notification delivery asynchronously.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Unbounded LIKE queries with no pagination could exceed 30 seconds on large datasets. No background job framework.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No pagination, no timeout handling, no async job processing.
findings.recommendation: Add pagination to search queries. Implement async job processing if bulk operations are added.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. No /v1/ URL prefixes, no version headers. Any changes break consumers immediately.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly.
findings.recommendation: Adopt URL-path versioning (e.g., /api/v1/tickets/) when rebuilding.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All service endpoints hardcoded in settings.py (database host 127.0.0.1, email host exchange.acme-corp.internal). No dynamic discovery mechanism.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hardcoded. No dynamic discovery, no externalized configuration.
findings.recommendation: Externalize endpoints to environment variables. Adopt AWS Cloud Map when on ECS/EKS.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Static files served from local disk with no CDN. No S3, no managed object storage, no document parsing capabilities.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems with no managed object storage. Single point of failure.
findings.recommendation: Migrate static files and attachments to Amazon S3. Serve via CloudFront CDN.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Raw SQL queries scattered in view functions. Django ORM not used. Each view creates its own cursor with inline SQL string formatting.
findings.gap: Database queries scattered with no pattern. No repository/DAO layer, no ORM.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Django ORM with proper model definitions and centralized data access layer.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 far past end-of-life (EOL November 2016). No version pinning in IaC. No documented update procedure.
findings.gap: Database engine far past EOL. No version pinning, no lifecycle management. Known unpatched vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS PostgreSQL with latest supported major version (PostgreSQL 16+).

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. Self-managed PostgreSQL with no disk encryption. Static files unencrypted on local disk.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest. Database data and static files stored unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS keys when migrating to RDS and S3.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: Django session-based auth middleware configured but no per-request token-based auth. Views appear accessible without login — no @login_required decorators.
findings.gap: No token-based API authentication. Views appear unauthenticated.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT authentication. Use Cognito with API Gateway authorizers.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Application uses Django's built-in auth. No external IdP integration, no SSO, no SAML/OIDC federation.
findings.gap: Application manages its own authentication entirely with no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or corporate SAML/OIDC identity provider for SSO.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: CRITICAL: Plaintext credentials committed to source control — Django SECRET_KEY and database password hardcoded in settings.py.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code. Deployment-blocking security issue.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: Rotate all credentials. Move to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy. Host OS Ubuntu 12.04 is EOL. No SSM, no Inspector, no vulnerability scanning, no hardened images.
findings.gap: No patching, no scanning, no hardening. EOL operating system.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to containers with hardened base images. Enable AWS Inspector for vulnerability scanning.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. Active SQL injection and XSS vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools configured. Pipeline has no security validation (no pipeline exists).
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (Bandit/Semgrep) and dependency scanning (pip-audit) in CI/CD with blocking gates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry. Debug via print statements only.
findings.gap: No tracing. No visibility into request flows or latency.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry when migrating to managed compute.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency thresholds, no availability targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability, latency p95, and error rate. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics. No business outcome tracking. Only debugging via print statements.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — no business outcome tracking.
findings.recommendation: Publish CloudWatch custom metrics for ticket volume, resolution time, SLA compliance.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no notification integration.
findings.gap: No alerting. Failures detected only when users report issues.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency. Enable anomaly detection.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No integration tests. No test files in repository at all. Zero automated test coverage.
findings.gap: No integration tests — no automated tests at all. Any change carries unquantified regression risk.
findings.recommendation: Establish test suite with pytest/Django test framework. Include integration tests in CI/CD.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No incident response automation. No runbooks, no self-healing, no automated remediation. Entirely ad hoc manual SSH and restart.
findings.gap: No runbooks — incident response is entirely ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create runbook documents. Implement auto-recovery on managed services.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no CODEOWNERS, no team attribution.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — no monitoring exists to attribute.
findings.recommendation: Define clear ownership with CODEOWNERS, team-attributed dashboards and alarms.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance
findings.description: No resource tagging. No IaC to define tags, no tagging standards, no cost allocation.
findings.gap: No tags on resources. No tagging standard, no cost attribution.
findings.recommendation: Include mandatory tags in IaC (Environment, Service, Owner, CostCenter). Enforce via AWS Config.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL. All business logic in application layer. Standard SELECT statements only.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false. This repo contains no IaC. CloudTrail is an account-level concern belonging in foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: Deployment Strategy
evaluations.reason: has_deployed_workload=false. No Dockerfile, no IaC defining compute, no deployment manifests in this repo. Deployment strategy cannot be assessed from source code alone.
